primitives.name: Assistant Coaching Consistency
primitives.verbatim_quote: The one principie never to be forgotten in portioning out the assistant's work is that no player shall have the style of his coaching changed during the season.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_{style}': 'dimensionless coaching style identifier', 't': 'time in seasons', 'P_i': 'player i'}
primitives.assumptions: Coaching styles are discrete and stable over time; player performance is sensitive to style variation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When C_{style}(P_i, t_1) \neq C_{style}(P_i, t_2), leading to performance degradation.

layer2.mapping: Enforces temporal invariance in coaching strategy through Bayesian update of player performance likelihood given fixed coaching style.
layer2.telemetry: Player performance variance across coaching style transitions.

primitives.name: Assistant Role Allocation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The assistants should never be permitted to coach the regulars.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A_j': 'assistant j', 'R_k': 'regular player k', 'C_{role}(A_j)': 'allocated coaching role for assistant j'}
primitives.assumptions: Regular players require singular, authoritative coaching; assistant roles must be segregated.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When C_{role}(A_j) = \text{regulars}, leading to conflict of authority and inconsistent instruction.

layer2.mapping: Maps assistant role assignment to a partition function over player sets, ensuring exclusive coaching domains.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of assistant-player interaction violations in training logs.

primitives.name: Coaching Style Stability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Early in the season the coach should study and decide on the best style for coaching each player, and then stick to it.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_i(t)': 'coaching style applied to player i at time t', 'T_{season}': 'duration of football season'}
primitives.assumptions: Stable coaching styles improve player adaptation; deviation causes confusion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \frac{\partial S_i}{\partial t} \neq 0, resulting in reduced player adaptability.

layer2.mapping: Models coaching stability as a constraint on the temporal derivative of player-specific coaching strategies.
layer2.telemetry: Change rate of coaching style per player over the season.

reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives form a coherent mathematical framework for modeling football coaching as a constrained control system. Assistant coaching consistency enforces temporal invariance in player instruction, modeled as a discrete-time dynamical system where player performance is a function of stable coaching style. Role allocation ensures hierarchical separation between assistants and regulars, represented by set-theoretic partitions. Coaching style stability introduces a temporal constraint on coaching evolution, preventing style drift that would degrade player adaptation. These operators interlock to define a dual structure: one of authority (role allocation) and one of consistency (style stability), both constrained by the principle of singular coaching per player. Failure modes arise when these constraints are violated—specifically, when coaching styles vary mid-season or assistants are allowed to coach regulars, leading to information leakage and performance degradation. The system exhibits a strong duality between individual player coaching and team-wide strategic coherence.
